unpeated-malt.summary: Speyside malts generally gain depth and sherry integration with age statements while losing some fresh fruit.

stages.label: Young (10–12)
stages.effect: Bright orchard fruit, honey and light vanilla; the barrel is a supporting player.

stages.label: Developing (15–18)
stages.effect: Dried fruit deepens, oak spice builds and the texture gains weight.

stages.label: Mature (21+)
stages.effect: Walnut, polished oak and marmalade; fresh fruit recedes into the background.

unpeated-malt.vintage: Cask type matters more than a couple of years' difference: first-fill sherry at 12 can taste older than refill at 18.

sherry-malt.summary: Sherry-cask Speyside malts generally deepen with age statements while fresh fruit recedes.

stages.label: Young (10–12)
stages.effect: Fresh dried fruit, bright sherry sweetness and lively oak spice.

stages.label: Developing (15–18)
stages.effect: Walnut, polished oak and darker fruit; the sherry integrates fully.

stages.label: Mature (21+)
stages.effect: Antique oak, marmalade and savoury depth; sweetness turns dignified.

sherry-malt.vintage: Cask type matters more than a couple of years: first-fill sherry at 12 can taste older than refill at 18.

heavily-peated-malt.summary: Peat slowly mellows with age while oak sweetness rises to meet it.

stages.label: Young (10)
stages.effect: Raw, aggressive smoke and brine; the peat is the whole story.

stages.label: Developing (16)
stages.effect: Smoke integrates with sherry or oak sweetness into a rounder whole.

stages.label: Mature (25+)
stages.effect: Peat softens to embers; dried fruit and polished oak lead.

heavily-peated-malt.vintage: High-peat bottlings vary batch to batch even at the same age statement.

bourbon.summary: Bourbon's age arc is fast by Scotch standards: oak extraction in new charred barrels front-loads the flavor.

stages.label: Young (4–6)
stages.effect: Bold caramel, vanilla and oak spice; the char leads and the grain sweetness is up front.

stages.label: Developing (8–12)
stages.effect: Oak integrates, darker fruit and leather emerge; many drinkers' sweet spot.

stages.label: Mature (15+)
stages.effect: Heavily oak-dominated; can turn tannic and woody — bourbon matures fast and can over-mature.

bourbon.vintage: Barrel entry proof, warehouse placement (higher floors cycle hotter) and mashbill matter as much as the age statement.

rye.summary: Rye's spice softens and rounds with age while retaining its herbal core.

stages.label: Young (4–6)
stages.effect: Peppery, herbal and bold; the rye grain's spice is the whole story.

stages.label: Developing (6–10)
stages.effect: Oak sweetness meets the spice; caramel tempers the pepper.

stages.label: Mature (10+)
stages.effect: Dried fruit and polished spice; older ryes read closer to a rich bourbon with a herbal thread.

rye.vintage: High-rye vs low-rye mashbills age differently; high-rye keeps its kick longer.

pot-still.summary: Irish pot still whiskey gains sherry depth and softens its spicy barley texture with age.

stages.label: Young (10–12)
stages.effect: Creamy barley spice with fresh fruit; the pot still texture is the star.

stages.label: Developing (15–21)
stages.effect: Sherry and oak integrate; dried fruit deepens the creamy spice.

stages.label: Mature (21+)
stages.effect: Luxurious weight: old pot still whiskey ranks among Ireland's most decorated pours.

pot-still.vintage: Cask type dominates: bourbon-led editions stay bright; sherry-led editions deepen early.

japanese-malt-unpeated.summary: Japanese unpeated malts refine rather than transform: fruit and oak gain polish with age.

stages.label: Young (NAS–10)
stages.effect: Clean orchard fruit and light oak; restraint already in place.

stages.label: Developing (12–17)
stages.effect: Mizunara aromatics (where used) emerge: sandalwood and incense over deeper fruit.

stages.label: Mature (18+)
stages.effect: Layered and delicate; oak recedes behind integrated fruit and spice.

japanese-malt-unpeated.vintage: Mizunara appears mainly in long-matured or premium editions (Suntory); a 12 without it ages differently.
